Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up items

Ava / Ben — thanks again for running through the prototype today. A couple of things I want to capture from our side so we’re aligned before a technical deep-dive: 

- Primary pain: our current embed + rerank pipeline is ~800ms median for a 3-doc retrieval + rerank, but tail latency spikes >2s during peak. This is causing UI jitter in search and poor user experience.
- Goals: get end-to-end request latency to <350ms median for query->rerank and reduce tail to <800ms; keep P95 <1.2s if possible.
- Features we care about: streaming token responses for long-context summaries; function-calling/structured outputs for extracting named fields from documents (claim, date, jurisdiction); local embedding cache and incremental rerank to avoid full recompute on small edits.
- Security: data residency + audit logging are required for pilot.

Can you send a short recap with proposed integration approach (SDK changes, whether function-calls are supported via streaming, fallback/quantization options), and a draft mutual action plan with milestones?

Leah will join the tech session if we agree on next steps. Best,
Samir

Ava / Samir — quick technical notes ahead of Wednesday’s call so we can focus on tradeoffs: 

1) Embeddings + rerank path:
   - We’ll recommend a hybrid cache + incremental rerank approach. Keep a per-document embedding cache in your infra (or Redwood Dedicated if you prefer). For small edits, we can rerank only the top-k candidates instead of recomputing the full set. That reduces end-to-end work by ~40% in our benchmarks.
   - Batching: Redwood’s runtime batches across requests and also supports dynamic batching thresholds — tuning will be required to hit the 350ms median.

2) Streaming + function-calls:
   - Streaming supports token-level output while still delivering function-call markers. In practice we emit "call_start" tokens when we detect structured output invocation; the SDK surface exposes a chunk stream and a final explicit function call object when the model finishes. Streaming lowers perceived latency for long summaries.
   - If you need strict field-by-field JSON as the model emits, we can enable incremental JSON frames (SDK option) but that increases CPU for parsing; we'll discuss tradeoffs.

3) Quantization and model variants:
   - For tail-latency control, recommend a two-tier model routing: a lower-cost quantized variant as fallback for heavy load, and a higher-precision variant pinned for canary traffic. This preserves quality while allowing predictable SLOs.

4) Security + audit:
   - We can provide an audit log stream (append-only) with per-request metadata for the pilot. For data residency, Dedicated or Private deployment options are feasible; I attached a short security summary.

Attachments: SDK patch (small interface changes for incremental JSON frames), MVP scope workbook, Redwood security summary (PDF).

I’ll bring a short demo of incremental rerank at the session.

Ben

Hi Samir / Leah — great conversation today. Below is a short recap of what we heard, agreed outcomes, and proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Please flag anything we missed.

What we heard (pain & goals):
- Latency: current median ~800ms; target is <350ms median for query->rerank, P95 goal <1.2s.
- UX: perceived latency for long summaries needs streaming tokens (reduce time-to-first-byte).
- Outputs: need structured, field-level extraction (function-calls) to populate claims metadata reliably.
- Ops: data residency and per-request audit logging required for pilot.

Redwood recommended integration approach (high level):
- Embedding cache + incremental rerank: maintain per-doc embeddings; on edits only rerank top-k candidates. Combined with Redwood batching this reduces end-to-end work.
- Streaming + function-calls: enable streaming with function-call markers; we’ll provide an SDK option for incremental JSON frames if you want near-real-time field emission.
- Fallback routing: two-tier model routing (quantized fallback) to control tail latency during spikes.
- Security: pilot on Dedicated (or Private if you prefer) with audit log stream and KMS integration.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed milestones):
1) Tech deep-dive & acceptance criteria — week of May 18 (owners: Redwood SE + ClearBridge eng)
2) Pilot scope finalization (MVP workbook attached) — due May 22 (owner: ClearBridge PM)
3) SDK patch and small integration changes (we provide patch + example) — Redwood target May 28
4) Pilot deploy (Dedicated instance + test data) — target June 4
5) Pilot validation & quality gating (latency/accuracy targets) — complete by June 18

Open questions / decisions needed from ClearBridge:
- Do you want us to host embeddings in Dedicated or keep them on your infra (impacts caching approach)?
- Are incremental JSON frames acceptable to your parsing pipeline (adds CPU, trades lower TTF)?

Attachments & links: MVP workbook (clearbridge_mvp_scope.xlsx), sdk_patch_v1.diff, Redwood security summary (redwood_security_summary.pdf). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1GvQb-example-doc

Next immediate steps:
- Samir / Leah: confirm Wednesday/Thursday availability for the May 18 deep-dive, and whether you prefer Dedicated for pilot.
- We’ll circulate a calendar invite with agenda and a short list of config knobs to test during the pilot.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Ava
